name: Arc-flash fibre loop sensor
summary: Bare optical fibre routed through switchgear that picks up arc light anywhere along its length.
description: A fibre loop sensor is an unjacketed optical fibre routed through busbar chambers or along switchgear lines. Light from an arc anywhere along its length enters the fibre and reaches the arc-flash relay, so one loop can cover a large area that would need many point sensors.

Because the whole length is sensitive, a loop identifies the zone but not the exact compartment, and the trip zone therefore follows the routing. Loop length affects sensitivity, and the symbol does not show routing, length or the loop-check function, which should be recorded on the layout and schematic.
readingNotes: Read the routing drawing to see which compartments the loop crosses.
Check that the trip zone matches the loop coverage.
distinction: A fibre loop covers a long area without locating the arc precisely; a point sensor watches one compartment.
